input.quote: Ono shall have the right (but not the obligation) to Manufacture and/or package, or engage a Subcontractor to Manufacture, Ono's requirements of particular Materials
input.rationale: The Agreement imposes no minimum purchase, take-or-pay, minimum royalty or volume commitment on Ono, and no volume caps on Ono's usage, so it meets the preferred position. Article IX frames supply as Ono's right, not obligation: Ono "shall have the right (but not the obligation)" to manufacture or source Materials itself (9.4(a), p0508) and "shall have the right to obtain from Array Ono's commercial requirements" (9.4(b), p0509); clinical and commercial supply is only "as reasonably requested in writing by Ono" (p0501), with forecasting and ordering mechanics deferred to future supply agreements. Payments are event- or usage-based: an upfront licence fee, milestones on first achievement, and royalties on actual Net Sales (6.3, p0422). The word "minimum" does not appear in the document, and the only "shortfall" (p0430) is a year-end royalty reconciliation true-up of amounts Ono has underpaid on actual sales, not a shortfall penalty. Any obligation to source requirements from Array would be an exclusivity point, not MINCOMMIT; no such take-or-pay obligation exists here. No redline needed; we should re-test this rule when the clinical and commercial supply agreements are negotiated, as forecasting/binding-order terms could introduce a commitment there.
